symbols.name: delay
symbols.summary: Simple `d` samples delay where `n` is the maximum delay length as a number of samples. Unlike the `@` delay operator, here the delay signal `d` is explicitly bounded to the interval [0..n]. The consequence is that delay will compile even if the interval of d can't be computed by the compiler. `delay` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: n
params.description: the max delay length in samples

symbols.name: fdelay
symbols.summary: Simple `d` samples fractional delay based on 2 interpolated delay lines where `n` is the maximum delay length as a number of samples. `fdelay` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: n
params.description: the max delay length in samples

symbols.name: sdelay
symbols.summary: s(mooth)delay: a mono delay that doesn't click and doesn't transpose when the delay time is changed.

params.name: n
params.description: the max delay length in samples

params.name: N
params.description: positive integer up to 16 (for higher powers of 2, extend 'primes' array below)

params.name: pathmin
params.description: minimum acoustic ray length in the reverberator (in meters)

params.name: pathmax
params.description: maximum acoustic ray length (meters) - think "room size"

symbols.name: fdelay[N]
symbols.summary: For convenience, `fdelay1`, `fdelay2`, `fdelay3`, `fdelay4`, `fdelay5` are also available where `N` is the order of the interpolation, built using `fdelayltv`.

symbols.name: fdelay[N]a
symbols.summary: Delay lines interpolated using Thiran allpass interpolation.

params.name: n
params.description: the max delay length in samples

notes: and the delay argument is at least `N-1/2`. First-order: `d` at least 0.5, second-order: `d` at least 1.5, third-order: `d` at least 2.5, fourth-order: `d` at least 3.5.

symbols.name: multiTapSincDelay
symbols.summary: Variable delay line using multi-tap sinc interpolation. This function implements a continuously variable delay line by superposing (2K+2) auxiliary delayed signals whose positions and gains are determined by a sinc-based interpolation method. It extends the traditional crossfade delay technique to significantly reduce spectral coloration artifacts, which are problematic in applications like Wave Field Synthesis (WFS) and auralization. Operation: - If tau1 and tau2 are very close (|tau2 - tau1| ≈ 0), a simple fixed fractional delay is applied - Otherwise, a variable delay is synthesized by: - Computing (2K+2) taps symmetrically distributed around tau1 and tau2 - Applying sinc-based weighting to each tap, based on its offset from the target interpolated delay tau - Summing all the weighted taps to produce the output Features: - Smooth delay variation without introducing Doppler pitch shifts - Significant reduction of comb-filter coloration compared to classical crossfading - Switching between fixed and variable delay modes to ensure stability

params.name: K (integer)
params.description: number of auxiliary tap pairs (a constant numerical expression). Total number of taps = 2*K + 2

params.name: MaxDelay
params.description: maximum allowable delay in samples (buffer size)

params.name: tau1
params.description: initial delay in samples (can be fractional)

params.name: tau2
params.description: target delay in samples (can be fractional)

params.name: alpha
params.description: interpolation factor between tau1 and tau2 (in [0,1] with 0 = tau1, 1 = tau2)

references: T. Carpentier, "Implementation of a continuously variable delay line by crossfading between several tap delays", 2024: <https://hal.science/hal-04646939>
